title: Server-side stitched preroll dynamically inserted into a downloaded podcast episode

source.name: IAB OpenRTB 2.6 Audio object (stitched, ssai) and AdCOM List: Feed Types
source.notes: All source records are retained in assets/sources.json by reference.sourceIds.

modifications: All IDs, domains, titles, XML and media descriptions are original test data.
Request/response IDs and impid are intentionally paired.
No real person, cookie, advertising ID, IP address or live tracking endpoint is retained.
provenance.sanitized: No production payload or PII used. All resource and tracking hosts end in .test; external network must remain blocked.

pairApplicability.note: Use x-openrtb-version: 2.6 when replaying HTTP; envelope itself has no version field.

specNotes: stitched=1 (Audio object) means the ad is stitched with the audio content rather than delivered independently; feed=3 is podcast (AOD, pre-recorded episodic content), distinguishing this dynamic-ad-insertion-into-a-download scenario from audio-web-26-live-exact-aac's live FM/AM stitched broadcast (feed=2). startdelay=0 marks this as a preroll, not the midroll/postroll slots already covered elsewhere in this corpus.

ssai=2 at the imp level (assets stitched server-side, tracking pixels fired client-side) is the Imp-level sibling flag to Audio.stitched; both describe the same server-side-insertion delivery model from two different object scopes.
No rule anywhere validates feed/stitched/ssai for audio (§3.3 of the audio/VAST map); this fixture uses spec-correct values so that gap is documented, not asserted as a failing expectation.
Validity describes protocol structure and declared constraints; generated media bytes must be checked against declared MIME/duration before playback tests.
Current Inspector contract displays VAST as inert XML; text visibility must not be counted as creative rendering or media playback.
notes: Core observations in the source archive were deliberately excluded from expectations. Protocol metadata may describe a vendor-specific 2.x carrier; it does not claim a normative minor-version inference.
